budget_rationale: g03's shape: one stated milestone plus a smoke run per cycle. Same iteration and token sizing as the gauntlet's small_app_feature_with_smoke orders, which are the only measured economics this repository has for a CLI flag.
goal: In the sample project, add a --width option to the CLI's report command that overrides the report_width setting for that run, leaving the existing precedence untouched when the option is absent, and prove it with a smoke run of the command.

dod: python3 -m sampleproj.cli report <dir> --width 20 renders at the requested width
python3 -m sampleproj.cli report <dir> without the option renders exactly as before
the full unit suite of the sample project is green
no file outside sampleproj/cli.py and its test changed
milestones.title: Width option implemented and smoke-proven

rationale: The small-CLI-tool capability, probed at a seam the project already half-built and never finished: report_width is a real setting in sampleproj/config.py::DEFAULTS and sampleproj/report.py::build_report already accepts width=, but sampleproj/cli.py::main never passes it, so the setting is unreachable from the command line. The order therefore asks for wiring rather than invention, and its proof is a real command run rather than a unit test, which is what separates it from the pure-code-change orders. It is deliberately not g03's --quiet flag nor g08's --dry-run: a bench order that restates a gauntlet order measures the same thing twice.
title: Expose an existing setting on the command line and prove it by running it
